page: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a dedicated x86_64 Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor operating at 3.9 GHz, delivering 64 physical cores and 128 vCPUs with hyper-threading enabled. Cache configuration consists of 48 KB L1 data cache, 2 MB L2 cache, and a shared 480 MB L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512 (supporting VNNI and BF16) and Intel AMX (Advanced Matrix Extensions) for matrix math, alongside hardware-accelerated cryptographic instructions like AES, VAES, and SHA-NI.

System memory consists of 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory clocked at 7 GHz, maintaining a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio typical of AWS compute-optimized instances. In memory benchmarking, large-block read bandwidth reaches 391.52 GB/sec and write bandwidth hits 167.99 GB/sec. The instance lacks local instance storage, requiring remote EBS volumes for persistent data. Dedicated network bandwidth baseline is provisioned at 50 Gbps, and no complementary public IPv4 addresses are included.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong parallel processing capabilities. The instance achieves top-tier results in PassMark CPU score (122,858.65), multi-core stress-ng (138,339.74), and multi-core Geekbench (22,872.0), driven by high core count and vector extensions. It shows top-tier performance in Clang compilation (68,652.0), multi-threaded bzip3 decompression (883.64 GB/sec), and PassMark extended instructions. In inference benchmarks utilizing AMX and AVX-512, prompt processing reaches 4,724.27 tokens/sec on a 135M parameter model and 368.28 tokens/sec on a 7B model. Static web serving throughput reaches 211.4 GB/sec, and Redis SET operations hit 209.47 million operations/sec.

The 2:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio represents an explicit trade-off prioritizing CPU execution density over in-memory database capacity. Cost efficiency is maximized for workloads that heavily parallelize CPU execution without demanding extensive local disk caching or massive RAM pools. It is suitable for compute-intensive batch processing, CI/CD code compilation pipelines, video encoding, CPU-based machine learning inference, and distributed scientific simulation.
description: Amazon Web Services c8i.32xlarge is an eighth-generation compute-optimized instance powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor and a 64-core, 128-vCPU Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz. It features 480 MB of L3 cache, Intel AMX, and AVX-512 extensions. The server is configured with 256.0 GB of DDR5 memory at 7 GHz (2.0 GB per vCPU), 50 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, zero GPUs, and no bundled local storage. Benchmarks demonstrate top-tier multi-threaded compute performance, scoring 122,858.65 in PassMark CPU, 22,872.0 in Geekbench multi-core, and achieving 209.47 million Redis SET operations per second. Memory throughput reaches 391.52 GB/sec uncached read bandwidth. Given its dense compute allocation and lack of onboard storage, c8i.32xlarge is best suited for compute-heavy workloads such as Clang software compilation, CPU-based machine learning inference, high-throughput static web serving, and distributed batch processing.
